guitar.modelsText: Dave Murray: modified 1957 Fender Stratocaster with DiMarzio humbuckers; Adrian Smith: Lado Earth
guitar.evidence: The studio recording features Dave Murray and Adrian Smith, not Janick Gers. Smith directly confirms Lado guitars, a 100-watt Marshall and possibly an Ibanez Tube Screamer for Powerslave. Murray's modified 1957 Stratocaster was used across the first eight Iron Maiden albums. Both guitar parts use bridge-humbucker-style tones.
guitar.notes: Target is the 1984 Powerslave studio recording. Standard E tuning is strongly supported by transcription and Iron Maiden's documented tuning practice, but no session statement specific to this song was found. Exact guitar assignment for every rhythm overdub is undocumented.
guitar.source: Guitar World, Adrian Smith on the making of Iron Maiden's Powerslave: https://www.guitarworld.com/features/iron-maiden-adrian-smith-on-powerslave ; Guitar World, Adrian Smith and Dave Murray 1983 interview: https://www.guitarworld.com/artists/interview-iron-maidens-adrian-smith-and-dave-murray-their-first-guitar-world-feature-1983 ; Powerslave original EMI liner notes

tone.target: 1984 Powerslave studio recording, core rhythm guitar
tone.profile: Layered British valve crunch with firm mids, controlled gain and clear pick attack
tone.summary: A bridge-humbucker guitar into a lightly boosted 100-watt Marshall-style amplifier. The sound is crunchy and layered rather than highly saturated.
corrections: replace signature guitars with period instruments

rig.name: Iron Maiden - 2 Minutes To Midnight - 1984 Studio Rhythm
rig.recommendedGuitar: Solid-body guitar with a medium-to-high-output bridge humbucker; use standard E tuning

blocks.purpose: Practical noise control without cutting sustained chords.
blocks.gap: Noise reduction is a GP-180 adaptation, not documented studio equipment.

alternatives.reason: Use only when the guitar or monitoring system produces more noise.

blocks.purpose: Approximate Smith's possible Tube Screamer and tighten the amplifier input.
blocks.gap: Smith described the Tube Screamer as possible rather than certain. Murray used different boost and distortion devices in the same era.

alternatives.reason: Use for a less colored interpretation of Murray's boosted Marshall tone.

blocks.purpose: Reproduce the documented 100-watt Marshall foundation with open British crunch.
blocks.gap: The exact Marshall head model and historical control positions are undocumented.

alternatives.reason: Use for a slightly softer and more compressed Murray-style response.
Use only when the GP-180 UK SLP lacks enough gain at practical output levels.

blocks.purpose: Provide the broad British 4x12 response required by the studio tone.
blocks.gap: The precise Powerslave cabinet speakers, microphones and placements are not reliably documented.

alternatives.reason: Use when a tighter and more focused upper-mid response is preferred.
Use when more upper-mid texture and speaker breakup are needed.

blocks.purpose: Practical compensation for FRFR playback and separation from the bass guitar.
blocks.gap: This EQ curve is a starting point, not a historical studio setting.

alternatives.reason: Use when its available frequency bands better match the guitar and speaker system.

improvements.summary: The stock rig covers the essential tone. A well-matched British cabinet IR offers the clearest upgrade.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Marshall-style 4x12 IR with a balanced dynamic-microphone position
proposals.reason: A quality IR can improve chord separation, upper-mid texture and microphone realism.
proposals.whenToUse: Use with FRFR, headphones or direct recording when the stock cabinet sounds harsh or flat.
proposals.expectedGain: More realistic speaker response and better layered-rhythm definition
